items.titleEn: Anthropic falls more than 9% day after record IPO
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Shares in Anthropic fell 9.5% in early trading Friday as the artificial intelligence company announced it had pocketed about $91.6 billion from its record-breaking initial public offering. The stock was changing hands at around $88 shortly after the opening bell in New York, down from Thursday's closing price of $97.17 but still above the $83 at which shares were priced in the IPO.

Buy the dip: Société Générale sees gold hitting $5,000 in 2027 despite sharp selloff
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Fears that persistent inflation will force the Federal Reserve to extend its tightening cycle into early 2027 have pushed gold prices down 8.5% this week, marking the precious metal's worst weekly decline since mid-March. Despite the selloff, one bank continues to view lower prices as a buying opportunity. According to its updated Multi Asset Portfolio outlook, Société Générale remains overweight in gol d heading into the first quarter of 2027, even as it takes profits in energy and reduces its broader commodity holdings. In its latest report, published Friday, SocGen said it had reduced its combined commodities and gold allocation to 15%, down from 20% in September. However, the bank maintained its 10% allocation to gold while cutting its exposure to global commodities to 5%.

Gold price trades near $3,568/oz after final Consumer Sentiment rises to 51.5, inflation expectations drop
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market is treading water after the latest data showed consumer sentiment in the U.S. improving in line with expectations, while inflation expectations ticked lower. The University of Michigan announced on Friday that the final reading of its Consumer Sentiment survey for November was 51.5. The data was in line with expectations, as the consensus forecast of economists called for a reading of 51.5. October’s final reading was 48. “Consumer sentiment rose about 7% this month, led by substantial post-election gains in both short- and long-run expected business conditions,” said Surveys of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu in the report. “Current personal finances improved for low-wealth consumers and, to a lesser extent, middle-wealth consumers, who experienced some relief with falling gas prices. In contrast, those with the largest stockholdings reported a decline in personal finances, consistent with continued AI-related agitation in stock markets.”

Gold heads for worst week in eight months as silver slides below $42 - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in early U.S. trading Friday, extending their recent selloff as a firm U.S. dollar, expectations for additional Federal Reserve interest rate increases and broad selling across financial markets pressured precious metals. Gold remained near its lowest level since September 2025 and was headed for its worst weekly performance in approximately eight months, while silver suffered heavier losses amid concerns about industrial demand and tighter financial conditions. Renewed tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz provided little support to bullion as investors continued reducing commodity exposure. Spot gold was trading near $3,558.20 an ounce, down $66.00, or 1.82%, while silver was trading near $41.650 an ounce, down $1.110, or 2.59%. Gold had traded as low as $3,513.70 during the session, while silver touched $40.990. Thursday's U.S. economic data reinforced concerns about slowing economic activity but offered little relief from persistent inflation pressure. Initial claims for unemployment benefits increased to 203,000 during the week ended Nov. 14, up from the previous week's revised 202,000 , while continuing claims rose to 1.763 million from 1.693 million. The Philadelphia Fed's November manufacturing index declined sharply to 6.3 from 20.9 in October , indicating substantially slower regional factory growth. However, the survey's prices paid index jumped to 58.2 from 43.2, its highest reading since April, highlighting renewed pressure on manufacturers' input costs. The figures followed earlier reports showing October retail sales increased 0.2%, industrial production declined 0.4% and building permits fell 7.4%. The combination of weakening economic activity and elevated inflation complicates the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook, with persistent price pressures continuing to limit expectations for a less restrictive policy stance.
